title: Polynomial-time closure under finite Boolean combinations
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $b_i$ be a Boolean-valued function on finite binary strings for each $i\in I$, and suppose the language of strings $z$ with $b_i(z)=1$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$ for every $i$. For any Boolean function $F$ on assignments of bits to $I$, the language of strings $z$ for which $F((b_i(z))_{i\in I})=1$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
hypotheses_covered: Each $b_i$ maps binary strings to bits
For every $i$, the language recognized by $b_i$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$
$F$ maps bit assignments on $I$ to a bit
replaced:
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set and, for each $i \in \iota$, let $b_i : \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean test on bit strings such that the language $\{z : b_i(z) = 1\}$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$, the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time. Then for every Boolean function $F : \{0,1\}^{\iota} \to \{0,1\}$, the language
\[ \{\, z \in \{0,1\}^* : F\big((b_i(z))_{i \in \iota}\big) = 1 \,\} \]
also belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
